notes:
Hardcore comes to Jedi: Survivor, the co-op menus get a settings screen and ready-up, your partner shows on the map,
and more of the world is shared between your games.
Both of you need 0.3.0 to play together.

**Hardcore**
- Every co-op journey is hardcore, as in JediCoop for Fallen Order. Fall in a fight and you're down, not dead: your
  partner has 20 seconds to reach you and hold Interact (E, or X on a controller) for 3 seconds to get you back up with
  half your health. Over a downed partner you see DOWN with the seconds left, and HOLD E TO REVIVE when you're close
  enough.
- If nobody gets to you in time, you spectate: you watch your partner play through their camera. Tap Interact to look
  around on your own, and again to go back to their view. Spectating costs the XP a death costs, as in the game, and
  you can win it back the same way.
- When your partner rests at a meditation point, your screen goes black and you come back at their point, resting
  there as they did.
- If your partner stands idle while you spectate, you can come back by holding Interact.
- Enemies leave you alone while you're down or spectating.
- If you both go down, it's the game's own death for both of you, back at your last rest. If nobody presses RESPAWN,
  you're brought back after about 20 seconds. If you fall to your death while your partner is still up, RESPAWN waits
  until they rest.
- When you aren't together (your partner is on another planet or not connected), a fall is the game's own death as
  usual.

**Playing together**
- Tutorial prompts that pause the game, like a tip that asks for a button, the DUAL STANCE ACQUIRED screen or the
  stance screen, pause in co-op as they do on your own and wait for both of you. A two-player sign with 0/2 shows
  under them and counts 1/2 and 2/2 as you each press; they close once you both have. If your partner is far away,
  down or in a scene, the prompt is yours alone and closes when you press. Prompts that don't pause never wait, and
  nothing pauses while one of you is down, so a revive is never frozen.
- Your partner's BD-1 now has its blue eye light.
- When your partner rides a nekko or hangs from a glider, you see it under them, moving as theirs does.
- When your partner meditates, they stay at the meditation point on your screen instead of disappearing.
- If your partner's game closes, they can join again straight away.
- Doors, lifts and other shared things no longer stop matching between your games after a fast travel or a long fall.

**Coruscant**
- On Coruscant's opening, following your partner, going to them or coming back after their rest never takes you past
  your own part of the story. If they're further on, you're told to catch up on foot, and UNSTUCK only puts you beside
  your partner when they're close.
- In hardcore on the opening, a fall nobody revives in time takes you back to your own last checkpoint instead of
  spectating, and a partner far away counts as not together.

**Co-op menus**
- When co-op is closed or you don't have access, HOST JOURNEY and JOIN JOURNEY show LOCKED, with the reason under them.
  If your access ends during a session, the session ends with a message.
- CO-OP SETTINGS in the lobby: ENEMY HEALTH, UNLOCKS, CHEST COSMETICS and HARDCORE, each with a line that says what it
  does. Enemy health and chest cosmetics can change any time; unlocks are set once the journey begins.
- Ready up together: when you go back to a journey you've played together, the host's lobby and the joining screen
  both have READY. Once you're both ready, a 5-second countdown starts the journey for both of you, and either of you
  can take READY back to stop it. A new journey starts as before: your friend joins once it has been saved.
- The joining screen shows the host's settings: enemy health, unlocks, chest cosmetics and hardcore.
- The lobby and the joining screen show a picture of the planet the journey is on.
- Trying to join a Jedi: Fallen Order journey from Survivor now tells you it's a Fallen Order journey.
- Long names no longer run off the edge of the follow question.

**The map**
- Your partner shows on the map: a pin with their name and how far away they are. When they're past the edge of the
  map, the pin waits at the edge, pointing their way. When they're on another planet, their name and planet show in
  the corner.

**The world**
- Lifts move in both games: when one of you rides a lift, it moves for the other too, and a lift stays where your
  partner left it. In co-op, a lift your partner moves doesn't crush you. Coruscant's lifts are still each player's own
  for now.
- The moving cargo in the Lucrehulk on Koboh, and the electrified ceiling climbs on the Shattered Moon, move in step in
  both games.
- Gates and platforms lifted or slammed with the Force, and ray shields turned on or off, change in both games.
- A rope shortcut one of you cuts down, or a zipline shortcut one of you opens, is there for both of you.
- Walls, vents and other things one of you breaks to open a way are broken in both games.
- Pots, jugs, barrels and the other things you can smash are shared too: what one of you breaks is broken in the
  other's game, and anything your partner broke before you joined is already broken when you get there.
- BD-1's dart targets switch in both games when one of you hits them.

**Finds**
- With UNLOCKS · SHARED, Force echoes, droid scans, lost treasures and Jedi upgrades one of you takes are taken in both
  games, and you both get them.
- Chests are always each player's own, whatever UNLOCKS says: you each open your own.
- CHEST COSMETICS in CO-OP SETTINGS: what's inside a chest is THE SAME for both of you (the default) or EACH YOUR OWN (a
  different cosmetic of its kind, one you don't have yet), chests you slam open with the Force too. A chest that holds
  a set, like a blaster's barrel, body and grip, gives you a whole other set. It can change any time.
- With UNLOCKS · SHARED, finds your partner made while you were away are given to you when you rejoin.

**Fights**
- A rest by either of you no longer resets the enemies close to either of you (within about 35 m): fights going on
  near you carry on, in both games. A downed or spectating player doesn't count, and if you both go down everything
  resets as usual.
- Loading in, or flying to another planet, no longer resets your partner's enemies, for the host and the joiner alike.
- In hardcore, when you come back at your partner's meditation point after their rest, the fights around you don't
  reset a second time: enemies stay as they were, in both games.
- Enemies a little further from the host (up to about 60 m) now move the same on both screens too.
- Your hits now land on enemies even when they're far from your partner.
- Enemy waves one of you triggers now appear for both of you when you're near (not during Coruscant's opening).
- If your partner beats a fight before you get there (the docks on Coruscant, for one), it's over for you too when you
  arrive, and the story goes on.
- XP for a defeated enemy goes to the player who lands the final blow. If you hit it but your partner finishes it, you
  get half its XP. Before, an enemy the joining player finished gave nobody XP. Bosses give you both full XP.

## 0.2.2

Fixes from the first online playtest.

- Your partner's outfit now shows in your game. Clothes they wear that you don't were invisible before.
- The joiner can finish enemies off. Before, enemies stopped at 1 health on the joiner's screen.
- No more invisible noise beside the host during fights.
- Enemies on the joiner's screen no longer jump about when they start moving.
- More enemies show on the joiner's screen at once in big fights.
- Enemies that turn up for the joiner (an ambush or reinforcements) no longer go missing in the host's game, and they
  join the fight instead of standing still.

## 0.2.1

Enemies now fight both of you, the way they do in JediCoop for Fallen Order.

- Enemies split between you and take turns. They come after whoever is hitting them, but never switch in the middle of a
  combo.
- Your partner's enemies are real in your game too: their swings hit you, so you can block, parry and dodge them, and a
  parry staggers the enemy for both of you.
- Hit an enemy that's busy with your partner and it may block you, then turn on you.
- Enemy blaster shots fly in both games and hurt whoever they hit. Block and deflect them as usual.
- Enemy footsteps, swings and blaster fire, and their flashes and trails, show and sound on both screens.
- Enemies that turn up during a fight (an ambush or reinforcements) appear for both of you.
- Enemies hold their blasters in their hands on the joiner's screen.
- The partner tile shows how far away your partner is beside their name.

## 0.2.0

The first co-op build for testers: play Jedi: Survivor together online. Early and rough: expect bugs, and tell us.

- Host a co-op journey from the title screen (ONLINE CO-OP), from one of your saves or a new game. Your friend joins
  with your code and plays your journey with you.
- See your partner in your game: their Cal, lightsaber, blaster and BD-1, with their name above them.
- See and hear what they do: their swings, footsteps and effort sounds, their saber ignition and BD-1's effects, and the
  sparks when they block, parry or deflect.
- No pausing in co-op: opening the menu or the map keeps the world going. Your partner's name shows IN THE MENU,
  MEDITATING, ON THE MAP or DOWN.
- When your partner fast travels, you're offered to follow them. When they fly to another planet, you're asked to board
  your Mantis and fly there from its holotable. At a meditation point you can go to the one nearest them, and after a
  death far from them you're offered to go back.
- Enemies: damage and kills are shared, and the enemies your friend sees move as they do in the host's game.
- Doors your partner opens open in your game too (doors they push or pull open with the Force as well), and automatic
  doors slide open as your partner walks up to them.
- ENEMY HEALTH in the lobby: how tough enemies are for co-op (Normal, Tougher, Toughest). New co-op journeys start on
  Tougher; the host can change it before beginning.
- UNLOCKS in a new journey's lobby: YOUR OWN (each of you keeps what you find) or SHARED (what one of you takes is
  taken in both games, and you both get it).
- Stuck? Open the pause menu and press U (or View on a controller) twice.
- The co-op chip shows your partner's name, with their planet and how far away they are, or what they're doing.
- Following your partner: while the screen is black, the place you're going to and who you're following show at the
  top left, and the game's own place card takes over when you arrive. Places use the game's own names.
- Pop-ups are smaller and don't pile up during a trip, and questions show the game's own key icons for keyboard or
  controller.
- Closing the game tells your partner straight away.
- Your Discord profile shows when you're hosting, joining or playing together.
- The lobby shows which region's relay connects you when you aren't connected directly.
- Offensive player names show as "Player".
- The first time your friend joins they play your Cal; from their next session on they play their own Cal, with their
  outfit, skills and finds. Cutscenes play for each of you on your own for now.

## 0.1.0

- The first early access build for testers. It doesn't add co-op yet: it checks Jedi: Survivor runs with JediCoop.
- Your Discord profile shows you're playing Jedi: Survivor as an early access tester.
- Turn that off in JediCoop.ini ([Discord] Presence=0) if you'd rather it didn't.
